texts: Each section file carries a metadata comment, an optional <!-- peek --> block shown while the section is closed, and a <!-- body --> block shown when it opens. The build script wraps them in the section chrome, so a section file contains only content.

<!-- id: architecture label: Architecture summary: One or two sentences, shown while the section is closed. --> <!-- peek --> ...the one diagram that makes this section worth opening... <!-- body --> ...the open markup...
Use the peek well. It is the only part most readers see. Put the section's key diagram, table or set of chips there, not a restatement of the summary line.
Use .panel → .flow → .node. Stack nodes vertically with .col. Label an edge with .arrow .at. Add a legend with .cap.

For an ordered exchange between parties. Four cells per row: step, from, message, to.
For score bands, tiers and thresholds. The left rail carries the tone.
One per document, at the top. It carries the single claim the document is making.
Lead with the argument, not the summary. If a reader takes one sentence away, this is it.
State it before someone finds it.
Wrap in .tw so wide tables scroll inside their own container rather than the page. Use td.n for numeric columns.
Pills carry the same three tones as everything else
Use .pill.n for a neutral, dashed pill
.grid2 or .grid3. Good for a two-way comparison.
Keeps moving, and the record must say so.
Use details.dx for depth inside a section. It keeps the top level to six sections while letting a reader go deeper.
Body content. Lettered rather than numbered, so it does not compete with the section order.
State the question as a question
Then say what changes depending on the answer.
A .note is a quiet aside with a left rule. Use it for a caveat, not for emphasis.
